source_text: Similia sunt autem somniis nonnulla etiam uisa uigilantium, qui turbatos habent sensus, sicut phrenetici uel quocumque furentes modo. nam et ipsi loquuntur secum, quasi uere praesentibus loquantur, <loquuntur> etiam cum absentibus quam praesentibus, quorum imagines cernunt siue uiuorum siue mortuorum. sed quemadmodum hi, qui uiuunt, ab eis se uideri et cum eis se colloqui nesciunt — neque enim re uera ipsi adsunt aut ipsi sermocinantur, sed turbatis sensibus homines talia uisa imaginaria patiuntur — eo modo et hi, qui ex hac uita migrarunt, sic affectis hominibus uidentur quasi praesentes, cum sint absentes et, utrum aliquis eos imaginaliter uideat, omnino nescientes.
orientation: Augustine is arguing that the dead do not know when the living see them, and he now extends the point from dreams to waking visions of the disturbed.
pass_a_gloss: But some visions of waking people are similar to dreams, people who have disturbed senses, like the frenzied or those raging in any way. For they too talk to themselves, as if they were talking to people truly present, they talk even with absent people as if with present people, whose images they discern, whether of the living or of the dead. But just as those who are alive do not know that they are seen by them and that people converse with them — for they are not really present themselves, nor do they themselves converse, but people with disturbed senses suffer such imaginary visions — in the same way also those who have departed from this life appear to people so affected as if present, although they are absent and completely unaware whether anyone sees them in an image.

lemmas.gloss: in an image, by way of an image

choices.why: Keeps the contrast with dreams explicit and preserves the literal sense of uisa as things seen.
Literal rendering of the idiom; keeps the physical-mental disturbance clear.

choices.english: as if they were talking to people truly present
choices.why: Preserves the quasi and uere force: the speech is only as if to present people.
rejected: as if in the presence of real people

choices.why: Cernunt is perceptual; 'discern' keeps the sense of seeing with the mind's eye, not ordinary sight.
Patior is passive suffering; 'suffer' preserves the sense that these visions happen to the disturbed person.
Omnino strengthens the negation; 'completely unaware' carries the total lack of knowledge.

pass_b_english: Some visions of waking people are also like dreams—people whose senses are disturbed, like the delirious or those raging in any kind of madness. They talk to themselves as if they were talking to people truly present, and they talk to absent people as if they were present, discerning their images whether living or dead. But just as the living do not know that they are being seen and spoken with by such people—for they are not really present or really conversing, but people with disturbed senses suffer such imaginary visions—so too those who have departed this life appear to people affected in this way as if they were present, when they are absent and completely unaware whether anyone sees them in an image.

last_rejected.quote: and they talk to absent people as if they were present, discerning their images whether living or dead
last_rejected.source_quote: loquuntur etiam cum absentibus quam praesentibus, quorum imagines cernunt siue uiuorum siue mortuorum
last_rejected.why: Missing 'etiam' (also/even): the Latin emphasizes they talk to absent ones *as if* present, not just that they talk to absent people.
last_rejected.fix: and they even talk to absent people as if they were present, discerning their images whether living or dead
last_rejected.ruling: 'etiam' is minor emphasis; core meaning preserved. Not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: completely unaware whether anyone sees them in an image
last_rejected.source_quote: utrum aliquis eos imaginaliter uideat, omnino nescientes
last_rejected.why: Latin says the dead don't know if someone sees *them* (the dead) in an image; English 'sees them in an image' is ambiguous but closer—yet 'unaware whether anyone sees' misrepresents 'utrum' (whether/if) as if the dead are unsure, when they simply don't know at all.
last_rejected.fix: completely unaware whether anyone sees them in an image-like way
last_rejected.ruling: 'omnino nescientes utrum' = completely unaware whether; English accurately renders both 'utrum' and 'omnino'.
